newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen dipping at open on U.S. GDP.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen dipping at open on U.S. GDP.

text.p: Toronto stocks were expected to open on a downtick on Wednesday as unexpectedly strong U.S. gross domestic product data dampened some of the euphoria that sent markets aloft on Tuesday.
"They didn't like the GDP numbers -- they've taken the long bond off," said one trader.
The U.S. 30-year T-bond was 19/32 lower at 94-29/32 to yield 7.04 percent.
U.S. first quarter gross domestic product rose 5.6 percent while the price index climbed 2.7 percent. The implicit price deflator increased 2.3 percent.
The TSE key 300 Composite Index rose 67.98 points to close at 5903.56 on Tuesday. On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 179 points to finish at 6962.
Most investors were looking toward Friday's U.S. nonfarm payrolls numbers for April as the most important indicator of how fast the U.S. economic engine was revving.
Nonfarm payrolls were seen rising 211,000 in April, while the unemployment rate was seen unchanged at 5.2 percent.
Canada's real GDP seasonally adjusted, rose 0.5 percent in February after rising 0.6 percent in January.
* MacMillan Bloedel Ltd said it cut its quarterly dividend to C$0.05 a share from C$0.15. The company said the dividend cut was in keeping with the current level of earnings.
